findings.summary: D122 was inserted inside D121, so D121 lost its Provenance bullet and D122 ends with D121's provenance.
findings.evidence: D121's bullets end with Reversal cost at 3003-3004. Then '## D122' starts at 3006. Line 3047 is D122's own Provenance, and line 3049 is a second Provenance ('the 15.4 minute median over 33 jobs ... cargo test -p xtask ... ci.yml'), which belongs to D121. This changes an existing decision record and misattributes provenance to D122. It violates the 'strangers' default.

findings.summary: Files changed outside the expected deliverables list.
findings.evidence: None of these are on the deliverables list. All are needed: new-field fixtures, record loading, the status priority source, the integration test and the record table. The critic's planned file list included them, so the impact is low.

summary: The code does what was asked. Urgent now ranks above high. A new command, `athena priority <job> <level> --why`, appends an `athena.priority/1` record and never rewrites the request. A shared `job_priority` function lets plan, drain and status all use the newest record over the reader's urgent mark and the request's text. The reader's urgency rule lives in the outputs.rs field doc, and reader.md is unchanged. Every targeted test I ran passed: plan ordering, the record override, the CLI integration tests (order and status flip, exactly one new priority-1.json, refusals that write nothing), the reading schema rule and the budgets test. Athena's fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. The verdict is fail on one documentation defect. In docs/decisions.md, D122 was inserted in the middle of D121, between its Reversal cost and its Provenance bullets. D121 has lost its Provenance bullet, and D122 now ends with two, one of which is D121's xtask/CI measurement text. Moving that one bullet back fixes it. Smaller gaps: no test shows the reader's `urgent_reason` carried from its output into the recorded reading, and several required files changed outside the deliverables list.
